name: A Lower Family of Order at Most Nine Has Two-Arm Holonomy
statement: In the terminal passive-gate setting, if $|K|\le9$, every lower holonomy cycle has length two. For its shores $S_1,S_2$, put $\varepsilon=|K|-|L|-6$. Then $0\le\varepsilon\le2$, and $\varepsilon$ is exactly the sum of the uncounted remainder, $|Z_0|-2$, all exponential incidence excesses, and $(|S_1|-2)+(|S_2|-2)$. Consequently $|Z_0|\le4$ and there are at most four distinct nonempty proper shores. If $|K|=7$, then $|L|=1$, $\varepsilon=0$, and the complete pendant two-arm normal form holds.
proof: The lower active slice is nonempty. A cycle of length $k$ therefore gives $9\ge|K|\ge|L|+3k\ge1+3k$. Since $k\ge2$, it follows that $k=2$ and the excess lies between zero and two. Substitution into the exact holonomy excess decomposition gives the asserted budget and its bounds on coordinates and shore types. At order seven every inequality is sharp, so the equality classification applies.
